criteria.description: Correctly explains that violating worlds get probability -> 0 as weight -> infinity.
Correctly connects this to classical hard FOL entailment.

solutions.fullSolution: As w_i->infinity, any world where F_i is violated by at least one grounding gets an exponent going to -infinity relative to fully-satisfying worlds, so its normalized probability goes to exactly zero: the formula becomes a hard constraint. A hard constraint that must hold in every possible world is exactly classical FOL entailment, recovering SYM-02's non-probabilistic logic as the infinite-weight limit.

criteria.description: Correctly describes MLN's weighted-formula specification and that both ground to the same factor-graph object.

solutions.fullSolution: A PRM is organized around a relational database schema: conditional probability tables for table attributes. An MLN is organized around weighted first-order formulas {(F_i,w_i)}, no database framing. Both ground into the same kind of factor graph/Bayesian network for a specific domain D, but MLN's formula-based framing is generally considered cleaner and more general.
